def generate_inputs(device):
    # Create position-dependent values that can't be cached
    predictions = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    targets = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    
    # Fill with unique per-run timestamp-based noise to defeat caching
    import time
    seed_val = int(time.time() * 1000) % 10000
    torch.manual_seed(seed_val)
    
    # First, ensure memory is 'dirty' with different values
    # Set all elements to produce small loss
    predictions.fill_(0.1)
    targets.fill_(0.0)
    
    # Now set last 256 elements (flat indices 524032-524287) to large distinctive values
    # Row 127, columns 3840-4095
    predictions[127, 3840:] = 777.777
    targets[127, 3840:] = -222.222
    # diff = 999.999, abs_diff > beta=1.0, loss = 999.999 - 0.5 = 999.499
    
    # Expected: first 524032 elements: loss = 0.005 (0.5 * 0.1^2 / 1.0)
    # Last 256 elements: loss = 999.499
    # Total = 524032*0.005 + 256*999.499 = 2620.16 + 255871.744 = 258491.9
    # Mean = 258491.9 / 524288 ≈ 0.493
    # If garbage = 0.005 (from fill): mean ≈ 0.005, diff ≈ 0.488
    # Threshold = 0.01 + 0.01*0.493 ≈ 0.015, diff >> threshold
    
    return [predictions, targets]

def generate_inputs(device):
    # Fragment memory pool to prevent reuse of reference's element_losses memory
    temp_tensors = []
    for i in range(50):
        t = torch.randn(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
        temp_tensors.append(t)
    # Clear some but not all to create fragmentation
    del temp_tensors[::2]
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    
    # Create inputs with massive loss in last 256 elements
    predictions = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
    targets = torch.zeros(128, 4096, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)
